c55884798371395efc741a432c24088d243a4c7c.boundText: - Test: `npm test` (`node --test 'test/**/*.test.mjs'`); e2e tại `test/e2e/rebuild-determinism.test.mjs` + `test/e2e/runner-loop.test.mjs` — bao gồm các kịch bản của hai stage đầu chuỗi, các kịch bản của stage lập-kế-hoạch (pass-through, chia-con-chặn-frontier, cần-người), VÀ 1 kịch bản S2-pull (submit → pass-through 2 stage → `take` người → một `fgos-runner --once` song song không giẫm claim người → người `return` xanh → `awaiting-approval`) chạy qua binary thật; round-trip cổng chờ-người tại `test/state/awaiting.test.mjs` + e2e CLI tại `test/cli/fgos.test.mjs`; unit tại `test/intake/{classify,discovery,plan}.test.mjs` + `test/state/{envelope,stage,store,frontier,work,replay}.test.mjs`; entropy-trend tại `test/report/entropy.test.mjs`. e3b5606060efbf880d94fec21cb8534355a12da8.boundText: | runner | RUL40 re-scope: herdr is never a source of truth or a delivery receipt for any fgOS state or Run outcome, but herdr's agent API (agent start / agent prompt --wait / agent wait / agent read / pane process-info) MAY be used by Dispatch as transport and as a failure detector (agent_not_ready, agent_prompt_stalled, blocked, agent absent). Truth stays with fgOS CLI state for Work and with receiver-written files (ack/result in the Run outbox) plus the liveness ladder for Runs. The former absolute ban on calling herdr agent start or reading agent_status is lifted; the ban on treating them as decision truth stays. | The 2026-07-18 ban conflated two rules. The measured bug (idle kills agent, airemote) came from trusting idle as completion, not from calling the API. transport.mjs herdrSpawnInteractiveAdapter already reads agent_status as its only completion signal, violating the letter of RUL40 while being unstable (false idle at 3.5s, mid-turn dips ~25%, multi-line prompt corrupting pane run argv). Upstream beegog v2.33.2 proves the stable shape: herdr agent prompt --wait as atomic submit-and-observe, receipt = worker-written ack file, result file outranks every herdr signal, agent liveness from pane process-info. Full investigation: docs/architect/proposals/visibility-and-interactive-contact-herdr-spawn.md sections 3.3, 4, 8, 11, 14 (H1). | 2026-09-06T09:58:26.819Z |

34c5dd4fdb2b2e55e030122913aea8461b3068f0.boundText: | p-2a39f940 | Neither fgOS trigger path (interactive pick, headless runner) reaches an MVP2-equivalent outcome on its own terms — different failure shapes, not equivalent | Case 1 (interactive /fgOS:pick, tsk-57u, docs/history/mvp2-scope-test-infra/reports/case-1-interactive.md) reaches all three literal artifacts -- green verify (23 pass/0 fail), a real commit (4f501f1) on the item's own fgw/tsk-57u branch, and a clean worktree teardown -- but fgos return's fresh-claim path measures only the ORIGINAL checkout's HEAD, never the fgw/<id> branch pick itself created, so return structurally refuses to register the completed work and the item is stuck at awaiting-human instead of proposed/done. Case 2 (headless fgos-runner --once, docs/history/mvp2-scope-test-infra/reports/case-2-headless.md) never reaches ANY of the three artifacts: fgos-runner.mjs resolves repoRoot via git rev-parse --show-toplevel with no override flag/env, dogfood-fixture is not its own git repo, so a real --once invocation would claim and dispatch real forgent work off the live repo/.fgos/state.json (8 real items) -- confirmed unsafe twice, never invoked for real. Fix scope: (a) fgos return's branch-aware path (bin/fgos.mjs:1306) must also accept a first, ordinary interactive pick's fgw/<id> branch, not only a re-claimed already-blocked item's branchHeadAtTake; (b) fgos-runner needs a cwd-rooted root override (e.g. --root/FGOS_ROOT) parallel to the fgos.mjs verbs' existing process.cwd()-derived isolation, so the headless trigger can be pointed at a testbed instead of always resolving through git toplevel. Done when both cases can independently reach green verify + commit on own branch + clean teardown AND the engine registers completion (proposed/done), proven by re-running this feature's two live cases. | proposed | mvp2-scope-test-infra |

a8ba5d7549494163bbea14377907ce24cc9cc6f3.boundText: | p-7eb9e65b | **fgOS and AgentKit (`ak`) overwrite each other's registrations.** Observed 2026-10-16 in this repo: installing the `ak` engineer kit for both `claude-code` and `omp` targets wrote the same rule set into `.claude/rules/*.md` and into an `AGENTKIT-OMP` block in `AGENTS.md` (read twice by Claude through `@AGENTS.md`, about 17 KB), and re-appended about 19 hooks into `.claude/settings.json` in its raw form next to the guarded form fgOS had rewritten them to (commit `036884908`), so each hook fires twice; `statusLine` points at paths that do not exist. Cause: two installers each assume they own `settings.json` and the instruction files, and each compares hook commands by exact string. Related doctrine: `docs/coexistence.md` (territory, one conductor per session, Known Gaps). | A written ownership contract between fgOS and other kit installers: each tool owns named files or marked blocks (e.g. fgOS hooks in `.claude/settings.json`, kit hooks in `.claude/settings.local.json` or a kit-owned block), neither rewrites the other's entries, and hook identity is the script path, not the command string; `fgos doctor` reports duplicate hook registrations and instruction blocks loaded twice (reuse `core/skills/instruction-audit/scripts/instruction-audit.mjs` logic) and `--fix` removes only fgOS's own duplicates; `docs/coexistence.md` Known Gaps updated; re-running `ak kit install` and `fgos setup` in either order leaves no duplicates (test) | proposed | — |
a8ba5d7549494163bbea14377907ce24cc9cc6f3.currentText: | p-7eb9e65b | **fgOS and AgentKit (`ak`) overwrite each other's registrations.** Observed 2026-10-16 in this repo: installing the `ak` engineer kit for both `claude-code` and `omp` targets wrote the same rule set into `.claude/rules/*.md` and into an `AGENTKIT-OMP` block in `AGENTS.md` (read twice by Claude through `@AGENTS.md`, about 17 KB), and re-appended about 19 hooks into `.claude/settings.json` in its raw form next to the guarded form fgOS had rewritten them to (commit `036884908`), so each hook fires twice; `statusLine` points at paths that do not exist. Cause: two installers each assume they own `settings.json` and the instruction files, and each compares hook commands by exact string. Related doctrine: `docs/coexistence.md` (territory, one conductor per session, Known Gaps). **2026-10-20 (owner machine, `forgentx-95`):** reinstalling ak for codex/omp/pi/grok again injected a 367-line `AGENTKIT-OMP:START:engineer` block into `AGENTS.md` (uncommitted; it blocked pulling main, so it was saved to `.fgos/runtime/config-backup-261020-1200/AGENTS.md.agentkit-omp-block.patch` and `AGENTS.md` restored). The same 8 rules also land in `.omp/rules/`, `.pi/rules/ak-engineer-*`, `.grok/rules/`, `.claude/rules/`. Measured: an omp worker (`unit-run-1792485257960-9c944a90`) loads only `AGENTS.md`; it does **not** load `.omp/rules/*` (no load condition), so without the block omp runs without the ak rules, with the block Claude reads them twice. Separately fixed today: `assembleSkills` no longer prunes third-party `.agents/skills` (COOK P4). Owner 15:42: handle in a separate session (INS lane; waits on the owner decision whether the 10-06 rule "do not modify ak/ck files" still holds and how to stay under codex's 32 KiB instruction limit). | A written ownership contract between fgOS and other kit installers: each tool owns named files or marked blocks (e.g. fgOS hooks in `.claude/settings.json`, kit hooks in `.claude/settings.local.json` or a kit-owned block), neither rewrites the other's entries, and hook identity is the script path, not the command string; `fgos doctor` reports duplicate hook registrations and instruction blocks loaded twice (reuse `core/skills/instruction-audit/scripts/instruction-audit.mjs` logic) and `--fix` removes only fgOS's own duplicates; `docs/coexistence.md` Known Gaps updated; re-running `ak kit install` and `fgos setup` in either order leaves no duplicates (test) | proposed | — |

59979bc3049033eacef99bd695268cc7cc0d439d.boundText: - [STR46] **Hợp đồng giao tiếp VÀO/RA của fgOS như một bề mặt I/O hạng nhất** — review chặt + hợp nhất các mảnh in/out đang rải rác theo từng stage thành MỘT hợp đồng mạch lạc, để bất kỳ transport nào (terminal, pane, chat, web, thứ chưa nghĩ ra) cắm vào đồng nhất và fgOS **chủ động được cả chiều ra**, không chỉ bị poll (chống "bị động"). Hiện trạng cần soát: chiều VÀO đã có cửa chuẩn (verb/CTR001, Host Adapter `b2d18cc7`, listener STR38) nhưng đường vào rải theo stage (submit STR14, answer/async-human-gate STR19, pull-door take/return STR26); chiều RA đang **bị động** — envelope + poll list/catchup + data_hash (STR37), log worker STR39, còn **đẩy/khởi-xướng (attention-envelope CTR008) thì deferred "chờ lực kéo"**. Việc: kiểm toàn bộ điểm in/out, chốt một hợp đồng in-out **tự-mô-tả** (vào=verb/CTR001 + identity gate; ra=envelope + attention/CTR008 push + self-description để thêm surface là dịch-transport→verb + đọc-envelope, không đường ghi riêng), và **nâng chiều-ra/khởi-xướng thành hạng nhất** thay vì phần phụ. **Câu hỏi CỬA-CHUẨN (escalate 2026-07-18, trong scope review):** bản thân "cửa chuẩn giao tiếp với người" CHƯA CHẮC là CLI-verb-spawn hôm nay — spawn-rồi-chết về bản chất không giữ kết nối để đẩy, nên "bị động" là hệ quả TẤT YẾU của model này, không phải bug. Ba mô hình phải cân: (1) CLI-spawn = cửa (b2d18cc7 hiện tại); (2) một **daemon nuôi MỘT cửa protocol chuẩn máy-đọc — không phải UI** (socket/JSON-RPC/MCP) để CLI+UI+remote đều là client, push/stream/remote thành bản chất — đây đúng là kiến trúc INTERFACE của herdr (không phải runtime của nó); (3) core-library + adapter mỏng (hợp STR41 executor-port), daemon chỉ bật khi cần remote/push. **CHỐT hướng 2026-07-18: model (3), Ở MỨC INTERFACE.** Contract chuẩn = **SCHEMA event-log + giao thức append/read/subscribe** (fgOS đã event-sourced), **KHÔNG phải một lib link được**. **Lib chỉ là CLIENT tham chiếu (Node) của contract đó**, không phải bản thân contract → daemon/UI-backend có thể viết bằng ngôn ngữ khác miễn nói đúng log-format (chống Node-monoculture, hợp mục tiêu substrate đa-app). CLI = adapter local dùng lib; daemon = consumer (xem chốt dưới); CLI standalone chạy đủ. **Chỉ code CÙNG-TIẾN-TRÌNH (CLI, TUI local) mới gọi lib TRỰC TIẾP; mọi UI web/mobile/remote KHÔNG chạm lib — chúng là client của CỬA MẠNG do daemon phơi ra → daemon là điều kiện CẦN cho bất kỳ UI ngoài terminal.** **Prerequisite móng:** tách core (verb-logic) thành lib gọi được độc lập CLI — refactor nội bộ, không đổi hành vi. **Phạm vi quyết định này CHỈ là interface (hình dạng cửa); tầng OWNER — ai ghi, đồng thời, lock CTR002, nguyên-tử STR45 — là layer RIÊNG, CHƯA xét ở đây.** **CHỐT thêm 2026-07-18: daemon RA KHỎI core — là CONSUMER giao tiếp QUA CLI** (`spawn fgos <verb>` cho ghi + poll `fgos list`/`rollup` + data_hash cho chiều-ra), KHÔNG link lib. Hệ quả: daemon thừa hưởng identity-gate + validation + single-door-lock của CLI miễn phí, không chế được đường ghi mới → **b2d18cc7 (Host-Adapter) được GIỮ + FULFILL, KHÔNG bị siêu-việt** (daemon chính là "lực kéo" mà CTR008 chờ) → **không cần decision-record-phá-luật.** Push nằm ở consumer sống-lâu (poll rẻ + giữ kênh outbound); core fgOS vẫn passive (chỉ CLI+log). Đây là **airemote tổng quát hoá** (consumer spawn-verb + poll + bridge remote). Sub-choice deferrable: poll-qua-CLI (đơn giản, một đường — nghiêng cái này trước) vs tail-event-log (push tức thì nhưng khoá log-format). CHỈ nếu sau muốn daemon **link-lib in-process** (3b) mới đụng b2d18cc7 → khi đó mới cần record. Kèm: **CLI tự nó phải chuẩn hoá lại** (verb surface + envelope + exit-code + self-describing schema) dù chọn model nào. Reference kiến trúc cửa đã có trong distill: `herdr:socket-api-control-surface`, `herdr:self-describing-protocol-schema`, `herdr:session-snapshot-bootstrap-rpc`. **Trước mắt (increment đầu, không chờ contract xong):** giao tiếp trực tiếp qua terminal/agent + vài pane thiết kế riêng show trạng thái work-item; nói với terminal-agent "vào tiến trình trả lời item X" / "vào exploring item X" rồi chat tiếp — chat modal item-scoped là client ĐẦU TIÊN của cổng. Là móng nằm DƯỚI STR38/STR39/STR40 và mọi UI sau; đứng trên STR37. Chất liệu distill tham khảo: `docs/distillery/deep-dives/herdr-vs-tmux-observation.md` (xưởng — vì sao surface là client của cổng, không phải runtime), airemote (path-allowlist/send-confirm cho bề mặt chat-untrusted) — done

5b44b9155aa29b9cac4f444da37e19c67399200a.boundText: - [STR60] **Bug thật: `fgos return`'s working-tree-cleanliness check (`isFgosOnlyStatusLine`, `bin/fgos.mjs`/`src/runner/merge.mjs`) chỉ loại trừ status line có tiền tố `.fgos/` literal** — tìm ra qua dogfood STR59 (cell `fgos-sample-testbed-2`, 2026-07-18): khi cwd nằm trong một thư mục con của repo git thật (vd `repo/dogfood-fixture/`, không phải root), `git status` báo path theo dạng `<subdir>/.fgos/...` (tương đối với git top-level thật), không phải `.fgos/...` — nên exclusion không bao giờ khớp, và `return` liên tục từ chối "working tree not clean" dù state store của chính nó vừa tự sinh ra. Workaround đã dùng (không sửa source fgOS): commit kèm luôn các file `.fgos/*` tự sinh của fixture trong cùng commit với code change. **Mở rộng phát hiện (cell `fgos-sample-testbed-5`, item `divide`, cùng ngày):** gate này KHÔNG chỉ vướng bởi leftover `.fgos/*` — `isWorkingTreeClean` scan `git status` của TOÀN BỘ repo thật (`repo/`), không giới hạn trong cwd/subdirectory đang chạy, nên BẤT KỲ file nào khác trong `repo/` đang uncommitted (ví dụ `docs/backlog.md` do orchestrator sửa song song) cũng chặn `return` y hệt. Phạm vi bug rộng hơn ban đầu: không phải riêng `.fgos/` path-prefix, mà là toàn bộ cleanliness-check chưa cwd-scope đúng cho một fixture nằm trong subdirectory — done

8581e528991b091675753683dd539389d5382b77.boundText: - [STR61] **Context continuity cho chat-in-the-middle & ngắt quãng dài khi item bị chia async** (nêu ra 2026-07-19, kèm 2 câu hỏi mở của người dùng khi cung cấp thêm input cho STR38/STR46): (1) work item bị chia nhỏ thành task con độc lập (async) — bối cảnh trao đổi người-hệ thống có bị giới hạn theo từng task con, không gộp được bối cảnh parent/sibling khi cần hỏi-đáp người; (2) trao đổi ngắt quãng dài (người trả lời rồi vắng nhiều giờ mới quay lại) — giữ session/bối cảnh trọn vẹn thế nào để chất lượng trao đổi không giảm. Người dùng tự nhận KHÔNG vướng ở cổng giao tiếp/transport (STR46/STR38 — cho là không phức tạp), CHỈ vướng ở lớp NỘI DUNG bối cảnh chảy QUA cổng đó — STR61 tách riêng đúng ranh giới này. Liên quan STR19 (async-human-gate: item đậu `awaiting-human`, câu hỏi/trả lời là một cặp ghi log, không timeout, không có khái niệm session/transcript) và STR48 (attention channel sống ở daemon-consumer, core vẫn passive). Chưa có khái niệm "sibling" trong data model hiện tại (`work-state.md:864` chỉ có `parent`/`deps`/`blocks`) — cần chốt qua exploring. **Chốt qua bee-exploring 2026-07-19 (`docs/history/str61-chat-context-continuity/CONTEXT.md`):** bối cảnh dựng lại từ state/log mỗi lần đọc, không lưu transcript; tự động kèm đúng 1 cấp cha (không sibling); chỉ báo "đã đổi" khi thay đổi ảnh hưởng câu hỏi/trả lời gốc, im lặng nếu không — done

cbc778982d3d1b2a8e5b298dcbc8a80605e5bdef.boundText: - [STR64] **[fgOS work — per decision `df90b761`, KHÔNG phải bee-tooling; mọi tham chiếu `bee-*`/`scribing`/`compounding`/`docs-manager` dưới đây là NGUỒN DISTILL, không phải đích sửa — xem compound-learn-enduser-docs's own decision on this]** **Reconcile map:** "scribing+compounding" → khâu compound-learn của fgOS; "skill export/docs-manager/documentation-management.md" → skill export/tích luỹ đọc-theo-tag của fgOS (CHƯA xây). **Đã giao (feature compound-learn-enduser-docs, ~slice 1-2, reviewed):** bước (1) taxonomy Diataxis + bước (2) tag `docType` capture-time + 1 doc how-to thật. **CÒN LẠI (lý do reopen từ `done`, per STR73 premature-done + decision `f5f7f6d3`):** bước (3) skill export/tích luỹ đọc-theo-tag (soát `docs-manager`/`documentation-management.md` trước khi viết mới, YAGNI) + bước (4) backfill; mới 1/4 quadrant (how-to). **[bước-3 shape locked 2026-07-21, decision `1d336d8a` / CONTEXT's locked decisions]:** bước-3 giao **INDEX đọc-theo-tag** (machine-readable, key theo quadrant + purpose/audience + source-capture linkage), KHÔNG gộp/viết lại doc; docs-manager/ck:docs/documentation-management.md đã soát — không tái dùng được, build skill fgOS mới. CoS bậc-3 diễn giải lại + **user-accepted**: index đóng bước-3, phần gộp tài liệu ("gộp sống") là slice sau. **Row KHÔNG flip `done` chỉ vì xong bước-3** (per STR73). — nguyên văn ticket gốc (design reference): **Compound-learn embodiment (p50-workflow-induct slice 2) + tài liệu hướng end-user** — p50-workflow-induct's own decision đã defer "compound-learn" sang slice 2 từ đầu. 7882787cd4cc6b294c483b97bb88f8104c1156f2.boundText: - [STR68] **`discovery.mjs`'s judge call can return prose instead of JSON when nested inside an already-running dispatched worker session, causing a spurious `awaiting-human` fail-safe park** (phát hiện 2026-07-20, trong p50-workflow-induct Phase 3 case-study, item `tsk-5gc` trong `dogfood-fixture`) — `judgeDiscovery` (`src/intake/discovery.mjs`) spawn `claude -p {prompt} --model {model} ...` (theo `.fgos-runner.json`) và bắt buộc stdout `JSON.parse` được thành `{clear: boolean, ...}`; bất kỳ lỗi nào (exit khác 0, timeout, stdout không parse được) đều gộp vào cùng fail-safe `{clear:false, question: DEFAULT_UNCLEAR_QUESTION}` — đúng thiết kế "không bao giờ coi phán đoán không chắc là pass" (module's own fail-safe comment). Nhưng khi lệnh `claude -p` này được gọi TỪ BÊN TRONG một phiên Claude subagent đã đang chạy (dispatched worker), model con đôi khi trả lời bằng văn xuôi thay vì JSON thuần (tái hiện thủ công, read-only: `claude -p "Reply with exactly this JSON..." --model sonnet ...` trả về văn xuôi từ chối, không phải JSON) — item hoàn toàn rõ ràng (`power(base, exponent)`, linear, không mơ hồ) vẫn bị park `awaiting-human` oan, không phải vì item thật sự mơ hồ mà vì lớp gọi lồng-nhau không ổn định. Full evidence: `docs/history/p50-workflow-induct/reports/p50-workflow-induct-6.md` §6 (Root-cause diagnostic) — done

3d4339920065ca3a42d823ca4d5c7c35ea355375.boundText: - [STR72] **Decision-supersession phải đồng bộ NGƯỢC về artifact nguồn (ticket/backlog/spec/CONTEXT), không chỉ ghi decision-log — nếu không, framing đã-bị-supersede tái xuất và tái sinh kết luận sai** (đào tận gốc 2026-07-21 từ hiện tượng "mọi phiên đọc STR64 là bee-tooling dù đã chốt fgOS"). **Root cause:** khi một quyết định đổi chiều (supersede), thay đổi rơi vào decision-log NHƯNG không lan về artifact nguồn đã gieo quyết định gốc — dòng STR64 trong `backlog.md` vẫn viết như bee-tooling, nên mọi phiên vào bằng entry-point tự nhiên (ticket ở mặt chữ) tái-suy kết luận cũ; bản sửa (`df90b761`) nằm ở artifact RIÊNG (log) họ không đối chiếu, và ban đầu còn chỉ "narrated in prose", chưa gọi CLI verb → chuỗi decision máy-đọc còn không thấy supersession một thời gian (phải tới `27052dd7` mới formal). Source cũ là attractor mạnh hơn một correction chôn trong log. **Áp cho fgOS y hệt:** một work-item đổi framing mà ticket/`docs/specs` không cập nhật → phiên fgOS tái-suy kết luận cũ; đây là năng lực compound-engineering fgOS phải có, không chỉ vá bee. **Đề xuất (cần bee-exploring shape chi tiết):** (1) supersede kèm bước bắt buộc "reconcile source artifacts" — cập nhật/đánh dấu ticket/backlog/spec/CONTEXT mà decision-bị-supersede đã trích; (2) hoặc backlog-row/spec mang con trỏ tới decision cai-quản, để người đọc thấy inline "framing dòng này đã bị supersede bởi X"; (3) consistency-check (grooming) phát hiện row/spec mâu thuẫn với một active decision đã supersede framing gốc; (4) supersede LUÔN qua CLI verb máy-đọc, không chỉ prose. — done

4cdc80a0eb6aff2f1fe176553a2f15944f1ecee7.boundText: - [STR94] **`pnpm add -g github:vantt/forgent` fails: `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED`** (renumbered from STR88 -- ID collision found at merge time: main's own STR88, from a separate unpushed session, is an unrelated fgOS-plugin verb-wrapper feature. Feature slug `str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle` in `docs/history/` and bee decisions is unchanged, internal-only.) (ghi nhận 2026-07-23 từ friction `.bee/backlog.jsonl`, layer `install`, người dùng báo lỗi thật + đồng chốt root cause với một phiên agent khác) — `package.json`'s `scripts.prepare` chạy `node scripts/install-git-hooks.mjs`; script này đã no-op an toàn khi không có thư mục git metadata (`repo/scripts/install-git-hooks.mjs:8-20`, đã xác nhận đúng) — **lỗi không nằm ở logic script**. pnpm 10+ (qua `allowBuilds`) chặn CHẠY bất kỳ lifecycle script nào của một git-hosted dependency trước khi chạy nó, bất kể script đó làm gì — nên mọi user dùng `pnpm add -g github:vantt/forgent` đều dính `ERR_PNPM_GIT_DEP_PREPARE_NOT_ALLOWED`, phải tự sửa `allowBuilds` trong `pnpm-workspace.yaml` mới cài được. Tái diễn với MỌI lần cài qua pnpm, không phải lỗi môi trường một lần; nhiều khả năng cũng ảnh hưởng các package manager strict khác (vd yarn PnP sau này) theo cùng cơ chế. **Fix đề xuất (đã thống nhất, per `str88-fgos-pnpm-lifecycle`):** bỏ `prepare` khỏi lifecycle tự động trong `package.json`; thêm `scripts.setup:hooks` (cùng lệnh) làm việc dev thủ công chạy 1 lần sau khi clone; thêm test chống-hồi-quy khẳng định `package.json` không còn `prepare` — loại bỏ hẳn trigger cho MỌI package manager, không riêng pnpm. Trade-off: contributor phải tự nhớ chạy lệnh setup 1 lần sau clone, đổi lại loại bỏ hoàn toàn friction cài đặt cho mọi người dùng cài qua git. Liên quan trực tiếp STR87 (cùng vùng install/setup) nhưng tách riêng vì đây là bug thật đang chặn cài đặt, cần fix độc lập, không chờ câu hỏi Rust-vs-Go của STR87. — done

---
name: fgos-run
user-invocable: false
description: >-
  Single execution driver for all domains: runs free-form requests, AgentKit plans,
  or specific phases through the Workflow runner and P1 Execution Core.
---

# fgos-run — Single Execution Driver

`fgos-run` is the thin driver for executing work across all domains. It does not own scheduling, merging, or execution mechanics directly — it delegates completely to the **Workflow runner** (`src/workflow/runner.mjs`) and the **P1 Execution Core** (`src/runner/execution/run.mjs`).

---

## 1. Input Modes

### Mode A: Free-form Prompt / Natural Language Task
When the user gives a natural language task or ad-hoc request:
1. Understand intent, scope, and affected files.
2. **One task → the one-liner.** Run it as one Unit straight from the prompt:
   ```sh
   fgos run "<prompt>" [--provider <id>[,<id>...]] [--persona <name>] [--capability <c>] [--rigor <r>] [--effort <level>]
   fgos run "<prompt>" --writes <path>[,<path>...] --worktree <linked-worktree> [--pattern code-change] [--input <path>[,<path>...]] [--verify "<cmd>"]
   ```
   Without `--writes` the Unit is read-only (sandboxed). `--writes` needs a linked worktree (create one with `fgos worktree create <path> --branch <name>` or `fgos worktree create <path> --detach`); from the main checkout it is refused before anything runs. `--provider` is a soft preference that `bind()` tries first and fails over from; `--capability` defaults to `execute`. `--input` hands the Unit repo-relative files to read; `--verify` is the command a reviewed run executes after each producing round (the preset pins none, so a reviewed run without `--verify` says it verified nothing).
3. **Several tasks → `--units`.** Formulate the **Unit** objects (schema: `src/runner/execution/unit.mjs`):
   - `id`: descriptive kebab-case identifier (a safe branch-name segment)
   - `objective`: concise semantic description of what must be done
   - `capability`: domain:verb (e.g. `docs:write`, `code:implement`)
   - `rigor`: `low` | `standard` | `high` | `critical`
   - `writes`: list of repo-relative paths or `*`/`**` globs the unit may modify (empty = read-only)
   - `dependsOn`: array of prerequisite unit IDs
   - `pattern`: `solo` | `reviewed` | `panel` (optional, defaults to config rule)
   - `verify` (optional): shell command a reviewed unit runs after each producing round; `skills` (optional): skill names the work needs, served only by executors whose `supports.skills` lists them
   - `prefer` / `persona` (optional, ad-hoc Units only): a soft executor preference and a persona name
4. Save Units to a temporary or workspace YAML file (`{ id?, title?, units: [...] }` or a list) and start them through the Workflow runner:
   ```sh
   fgos workflow start --units <units-file.yaml> [--effort <level>]
   ```
   A writing Unit that depends on exactly one writing Unit starts from that Unit's branch; nothing is merged automatically (`fgos workflow status` lists `writeBranches`).

### Mode B: AgentKit Plan Execution
When the user asks to run a plan, a phase ("run phase 2"), or a phase range ("run phase 1..3"), the plan is an input you read, not something the runner translates:
1. Read the plan and the phase files as artifacts. Verify the phase's units with plan-lint:
   ```sh
   fgos plan-lint <planPath> --phase <N> --json
   ```
2. Choose a bounded wave of Units for the phase yourself (what can run now, in what order, what each one may write) and run them through one of the two doors:
   ```sh
   fgos run "<objective>" --writes <paths> --worktree <linked-worktree>
   fgos workflow start --units <file> [--foreground]
   ```
   `--units` takes a YAML or JSON list of Units, one step per Unit, ordered by each Unit's `dependsOn`.
   `start` returns at once with the `workflowRunId` and a `detached` block; the run continues in a
   detached process. Read progress with `fgos workflow status <workflowRunId>` (or pass `--foreground`
   to wait in place); `fgos workflow answer` and `fgos workflow resume` return the same way. Do not treat
   the output of `start`, `answer` or `resume` as the final state.
3. Each Unit runs via `fgos run` in its own isolated worktree and integrates changes cleanly using pure git. `fgos workflow start --plan` no longer exists; a later conductor skill (`fgos-cook`) will own whole-plan execution on a case.

---

## 2. Human Review Gates & Question Batching

When a workflow step declares a human gate (`gate: { kind: "human" }`) or when an owner review is required:
1. The Workflow runner parks at the gate with outcome `parked` and records the pending question(s).
2. `fgos-run` gathers **all open questions across all parked steps** into a single structured batch; each question follows the decision-question template (`../_shared/decision-question.md`).
3. The user answers all questions in one interaction.
4. Answers are recorded via:
   ```sh
   fgos workflow answer <workflowRunId> --step <stepId> --answer "<response>"
   ```
5. The runner resumes execution automatically.

---

## 3. Execution Invariants

- **G2 Non-Infrastructure:** Units, presets, plans, and driver prompts never pin executors, providers, models, tiers, or invocations; an ad-hoc Unit (one-liner `--provider`, `prefer` in a `--units` file) may carry a soft `prefer` that `bind()` tries first and fails over from. Only a human `--override` pins; everything else is resolved by `bind()`.
- **Runner Commits, Worker Does Not:** A writing Unit's brief lists its write scope; the worker edits files and stops, never running `git add`/`git commit`. After a passing round the runner commits only paths inside the Unit's `writes` (subject from the first line of the worker's `summary`); a path the worker needs outside that scope goes in `needsWrites`, not on disk.
- **G7 Herdr Default:** All out-of-process unit runs default to spawning in a watched `herdr` terminal pane when herdr is available, falling back to `cli` when headless.
- **Fail-Closed Mutating Gate:** Every file mutation runs strictly inside an isolated linked git worktree matching the Unit run specification.
- **Honest Outcomes:** Reviewer findings are tracked as `findings`, not execution failures, and fix rounds are bounded by the collaboration pattern.

---

## 4. Reviewing a Change That Touches Tests

Every behaviour has one owning proof (AGENTS.md L5 question 5, design principle 8 **One proof**). Whoever reviews a Unit's result, or accepts a lead's report, checks these four lines and returns a finding for each one that fails; a report that adds tests without reasons, or deletes a mechanism without a retired list, is not accepted:

1. **Every new test file:** why not the existing file for this module? Only a new module or a new boundary gets a new file.
2. **Every new test:** its title names the behaviour in plain words (no task ids), the owning proof was searched for (`rg` the behaviour's words and the symbol), and the report gives the reason no existing test proves it.
3. **Every deleted or replaced mechanism:** its tests are retired in the same change and listed, each with the test that now owns the behaviour or the statement that the behaviour is gone.
4. **Every Node test in a Rust-ported area** (git, holder-lock, event-store, run-supervisor, terminal-control): it is the one route proof for its port or a Node-only behaviour, never a copy of a case a Rust test owns.

The report quotes the `suite:` line `npm test` prints (files, `test()` calls, wall time against `test/suite-baseline.json`).

# Project Rules

Every agent CLI used on this repository (Claude Code, Codex, omp, pi, agy)
reads one shared instruction file: AGENTS.md. Claude Code reads AGENTS.md on
its own only when no CLAUDE.md exists, so this file stays and does nothing but
import it. Put every rule in AGENTS.md, never here; a tool that writes its own
block into this file (for example `gitnexus analyze`) makes Claude read that
block twice. The bare import below must never be wrapped in backticks; that
disables it.

@AGENTS.md

538150c576e58a63d3f4052b3fdcc93402f1f1c0.boundText:
1. **Verify Real Commit:** Directly inspect git history in the worktree (`git -C "$wt" log -1 --stat`) to verify substantive changes were committed.
2. **Verify Clean Tree:** Verify `git -C "$wt" status --porcelain` is clean (all worker edits committed).
3. **Execute Verification Directly:** The driver runs the required focused test command directly in the worktree, asserting exit code 0 and all assertions passing.

# Shared Fragment: Coding-Cell Policy

This coding-domain fragment defines the technical policy for executing any mutating coding cell — whether a standalone single-cell change (via `fgos-run`) or one step within an implementation track. It is completely self-contained and makes no assumptions about multi-cell tracks, plans, or multi-cell status tables.

---

## 1. Isolated Worktree Discipline

Every mutating coding Unit must execute inside its own dedicated git worktree on its own dedicated branch:

1. **Main Checkout Protection:**
   The fgOS execution core strictly forbids mutating execution in the main checkout: any mutating dispatch where `--cwd` resolves to the repository root is hard-refused.
2. **Canonical Lifecycle Procedure:**
   The exact shell procedure for opening, branch reuse without `-b`, `$base` recording, objective-text branch guards, and cleanup is defined in [`private-cell-worktree.md`](private-cell-worktree.md). Coding cells follow that procedure without variation:
   - Worktree path: `../<prefix>-<slug>` (outside the main checkout directory).
   - Branch: `<prefix>--<slug>` (isolated branch derived from target base branch).
   - Dependency initialization: Run dependencies install (e.g. `npm ci`) inside the worktree so test commands execute reliably.
3. **Pre-Dispatch Verification:**
   Before executing any mutating command, the driver must verify:
   - CWD is not the main checkout.
   - Current branch is the designated cell branch.
   - Working tree is clean (`git status --porcelain` empty).
4. **Explicit CWD Passing:**
   Every mutating command (`fgos run`, `fgos workflow start`) must explicitly pass `--cwd <worktree-path>`.

---

## 2. Proof Tiers

Every coding cell must declare and satisfy a definite proof tier:

| Proof Tier | Scope | When Required |
|---|---|---|
| **Tier 1: Focused** | Targeted test suites directly exercising the touched symbols, interfaces, and contracts. | Required for every mutating cell. Must run inside the cell worktree and exit 0. |
| **Tier 2: Affected** | Subsystem and integration tests covering the blast radius of callers, dependents, and contracts. | Required when changing shared utilities, exported APIs, or core dispatch/coordination interfaces. |
| **Tier 3: Full-Suite Gate** | The full repository test suite (`npm test`). | Required when touching platform foundation invariants, isolation-breaking paths, or when independent review escalates a proof gap to full. |

### Test-Selection Block

Declare once per cell and inline the real command into every produce/revise/recheck objective (a dispatched worker sees only its own objective, never a driver's private notes):

```text
FOCUSED_TESTS: <command(s) for the changed module/symbol/behavior>
AFFECTED_TESTS: <command(s) covering the blast radius, or "same-as-focused">
FULL_TEST: <the project's whole test command>
DECISION: focused: <cmd>; affected: <cmd|same-as-focused>; full: <deferred-to-final-gate|triggered (<category>)|required (<reason>)>
```

**`FULL_TRIGGERS` (mechanical, fire regardless of the declared tier):** dispatch/self-host hooks; session/replay/schema core; shared invariants; migrations; test-harness foundations; package manifest/install/release-boundary scripts.

**Full suite runs once per `(tree, environment)` state, never mechanically per round.** Reuse a proof result under this key instead of re-running:

```text
proof key = (command, git rev-parse <ref>^{tree}, environment fingerprint)
```

Record the fingerprint (toolchain/lockfile/prerequisite versions) alongside the key -- two runs on an identical tree with no recorded fingerprint for either cannot be compared, so reuse is never claimed without one.

### Reviewer/Red-Team Inspect Proof by Default

Reviewer and red-team default to inspecting the recorded proof (command, tree hash, fingerprint), never re-running it, unless: the proof is stale (tree hash or fingerprint changed since it was recorded), the proof is insufficient (the declared tier does not exercise the changed contract), or a specific counterexample needs fresh output to demonstrate. An insufficient tier is a finding naming the gap -- reviewer/red-team judge sufficiency, they never self-escalate to a wider tier themselves.

### Known Engine Limit: Proof Tiers Are Lead Discipline, Not Schema-Enforced

The unit / workflow run schema has no field for a proof tier, `FULL_TRIGGERS`, or an environment fingerprint, and `disposition`/`rationale` accepts any non-empty string regardless of what it claims. A driver who does not actually run `FULL_TEST`, or who mislabels a real regression as `environmental-precondition`, is not caught by anything the runner checks -- this section is entirely Lead discipline in prose, not an enforced gate.

---

## 3. Independent Verification of Doer Commit and Tests

The driver must never accept worker self-narration, conversational claims, or ungrounded status reports:

1. **Verify Real Commit:** Directly inspect git history in the worktree (`git -C "$wt" log -1 --stat`) to verify substantive changes were committed.
2. **Verify Clean Tree:** Verify `git -C "$wt" status --porcelain` is clean (all worker edits committed).
3. **Execute Verification Directly:** The driver runs the required focused test command directly in the worktree, asserting exit code 0 and all assertions passing.
4. **Caveat Rule:** Caveats reported by reviewer or red-team operations block session completion and require uncaveated re-execution per driver discipline Step 4.

---

## 4. Merge and Cleanup Only After Explicit Completion

The sequence between Unit run / Workflow run completion and git branch integration is strictly ordered:

```text
run completed
  -> verify run status: pass / completed
  -> git merge --no-ff <cell-branch> (into target branch)
  -> git worktree remove <worktree-path>
```

1. **No Run Git Authority:** A Unit run possesses zero git merge authority. Merging into the base/target branch is strictly a driver action performed outside the unit run.
2. **Completion Before Merge:** The driver must never merge a cell branch into the target branch until the run has succeeded and reflects `status: "completed"` / `outcome: "pass"`.
3. **Post-Close Cleanup:** After the merge commit is verified on the target branch, the cell worktree and temporary branch may be removed.

---

## 5. Tested and Integrated Identity

Every merged coding cell produces two distinct commit identities:

- **`testedSha`:** The exact commit SHA in the cell worktree where all declared proof tier tests executed and passed.
- **`integratedSha`:** The resulting commit SHA on the target branch after integration (merge commit or rebased tip).

### Non-Inference Rule

If `testedSha !== integratedSha`, proof passed on the worktree cannot be inferred to hold on the target branch. **Tree-Identity Exception:** If and only if `git diff <testedSha> <integratedSha> -- .` is completely empty (no tracked content changes) **and** the environment fingerprint (toolchain, lockfile, built prerequisites) is identical, the driver may record `treeIdentical: true` and certify completion from the pre-merge run. Otherwise: re-run `AFFECTED_TESTS` against `integratedSha` at minimum, escalating to `FULL_TEST` when a `FULL_TRIGGERS` category fired against the merged diff (`git diff <preMergeBase> <integratedSha>`, not just the cell's own diff -- a moved target branch can trigger it too).

### Post-Merge Verification (required before cleanup)

Record the outcome of the check above as an ordinary, tracked `--allow-empty` commit naming `testedSha`, `integratedSha`, and the result -- never a `git note` (`refs/notes/*` is outside the default commit graph and does not push/fetch by default, so it is not durable at the project level). Immediately before removing the worktree or branch, re-assert `HEAD` still equals that commit: another writer could have advanced the target branch in the meantime.

disables it.

@AGENTS.md

6ac323e783157043f4c21d1197ef5d751d1c567d.boundText: - [STR67] **Goal-directed planning: người dùng khai MVP/milestone, fgOS tự sắp xếp việc hướng tới nó nhanh nhất** (nêu ra + escalate 2026-07-20, trong lúc bàn P50 và soạn câu MVP nháp cho chính fgOS) — KHÔNG phải thói quen roadmap nội bộ của team fgOS, mà là **tính năng sản phẩm cấp cho người dùng cuối**: một người dùng fgOS xây agent app của họ tự khai mục tiêu (MVP/milestone) của dự án HỌ, và fgOS tự sắp xếp/ưu tiên backlog hướng tới mục tiêu đó nhanh nhất — câu MVP nháp của chính fgOS (`docs/history/p50-workflow-induct/reports/...` artifact 2026-07-20) trở thành ca dogfood ĐẦU TIÊN của chính tính năng này, không phải một quyết định nội bộ rời rạc. **Đã có building block liên quan** trong `work-graph-intelligence` (`src/state/graph-metrics.mjs`): `criticalPath(view)` (chuỗi phụ thuộc dài nhất, số bước tối thiểu) và `greedyTopUnblock(view, k)` (greedy xếp hạng việc chưa xong theo mức mở-khoá, thuật toán submodular-cover) — cả hai hiện tính trên TOÀN BỘ graph ("mở khoá mọi thứ"); tính năng mới cần biến thể SCOPED THEO GOAL (chỉ xếp hạng việc nằm trên đường tới một target đã khai, không phải mọi thứ). Cần bee-exploring riêng trước khi shape — còn gray-area thật: "goal" là work-item hay entity mới? liên hệ thế nào với dep-graph/parent hiện có? — done

f8b1aee796fc246ec5b3faf5f4c755b9341a196f.boundText: - [STR68] **`discovery.mjs`'s judge call can return prose instead of JSON when nested inside an already-running dispatched worker session, causing a spurious `awaiting-human` fail-safe park** (phát hiện 2026-07-20, trong p50-workflow-induct Phase 3 case-study, item `tsk-5gc` trong `dogfood-fixture`) — `judgeDiscovery` (`src/intake/discovery.mjs`) spawn `claude -p {prompt} --model {model} ...` (theo `.fgos-runner.json`) và bắt buộc stdout `JSON.parse` được thành `{clear: boolean, ...}`; bất kỳ lỗi nào (exit khác 0, timeout, stdout không parse được) đều gộp vào cùng fail-safe `{clear:false, question: DEFAULT_UNCLEAR_QUESTION}` — đúng thiết kế "không bao giờ coi phán đoán không chắc là pass" (module's own fail-safe comment). Nhưng khi lệnh `claude -p` này được gọi TỪ BÊN TRONG một phiên Claude subagent đã đang chạy (dispatched worker), model con đôi khi trả lời bằng văn xuôi thay vì JSON thuần (tái hiện thủ công, read-only: `claude -p "Reply with exactly this JSON..." --model sonnet ...` trả về văn xuôi từ chối, không phải JSON) — item hoàn toàn rõ ràng (`power(base, exponent)`, linear, không mơ hồ) vẫn bị park `awaiting-human` oan, không phải vì item thật sự mơ hồ mà vì lớp gọi lồng-nhau không ổn định. Full evidence: `docs/history/p50-workflow-induct/reports/p50-workflow-induct-6.md` §6 (Root-cause diagnostic) — done

d8d1ef0e59fd0513b225f1bb99724baa4569d0f5.boundText: - [STR72] **Decision-supersession phải đồng bộ NGƯỢC về artifact nguồn (ticket/backlog/spec/CONTEXT), không chỉ ghi decision-log — nếu không, framing đã-bị-supersede tái xuất và tái sinh kết luận sai** (đào tận gốc 2026-07-21 từ hiện tượng "mọi phiên đọc STR64 là bee-tooling dù đã chốt fgOS"). **Root cause:** khi một quyết định đổi chiều (supersede), thay đổi rơi vào decision-log NHƯNG không lan về artifact nguồn đã gieo quyết định gốc — dòng STR64 trong `backlog.md` vẫn viết như bee-tooling, nên mọi phiên vào bằng entry-point tự nhiên (ticket ở mặt chữ) tái-suy kết luận cũ; bản sửa (`df90b761`) nằm ở artifact RIÊNG (log) họ không đối chiếu, và ban đầu còn chỉ "narrated in prose", chưa gọi CLI verb → chuỗi decision máy-đọc còn không thấy supersession một thời gian (phải tới `27052dd7` mới formal). Source cũ là attractor mạnh hơn một correction chôn trong log. **Áp cho fgOS y hệt:** một work-item đổi framing mà ticket/`docs/specs` không cập nhật → phiên fgOS tái-suy kết luận cũ; đây là năng lực compound-engineering fgOS phải có, không chỉ vá bee. **Đề xuất (cần bee-exploring shape chi tiết):** (1) supersede kèm bước bắt buộc "reconcile source artifacts" — cập nhật/đánh dấu ticket/backlog/spec/CONTEXT mà decision-bị-supersede đã trích; (2) hoặc backlog-row/spec mang con trỏ tới decision cai-quản, để người đọc thấy inline "framing dòng này đã bị supersede bởi X"; (3) consistency-check (grooming) phát hiện row/spec mâu thuẫn với một active decision đã supersede framing gốc; (4) supersede LUÔN qua CLI verb máy-đọc, không chỉ prose. — done

# Bootstrap and lane — full mechanics

The full detail behind SKILL.md's Step 1.

## Read CONTEXT.md

Read the item's `docsRef` field to find `docs/history/<feature>/`, then
read that feature's `CONTEXT.md` — the locked decisions are the only
source of truth for what this plan can assume. If a critical-patterns or
prior-learnings doc exists for this product area, read it too; a
precedent already solved beats research.

## Register a freshly-created feature dir's `docsRef` immediately

When `docsRef` is empty — most commonly an item whose discovery verdict
was `clear`, which skips `exploring` and therefore never gets a
`CONTEXT.md`/`docsRef` written for it — this skill still picks a
`docs/history/<feature>/` path of its own (a descriptive feature-slug is
fine; nothing here forces `<feature>` to equal the item id). The moment
that path is decided, BEFORE writing anything into it (`plan.md`,
`RESEARCH.md` from a `fgos-researching` call, etc.), register it on the
item:

```bash
fgos edit "<item-id>" --docs-ref "docs/history/<feature>/"
```

Skip this call when `docsRef` is already set — never overwrite a value
that already points somewhere real. Without it, `fgos approve`'s own
heavy-tier gate has no way to find `plan.md` unless `<feature>` happens
to equal the item id by coincidence — a real refusal one session hit
live, worked around there with a manual `git mv` to the item-id path.
`fgos-coding-exploring`'s own CONTEXT.md-creation step registers `docsRef`
the same way, at the same trigger.

## Reclaim the ball if it isn't yours

Check `data.work[id].holder` (`fgos list --id <id> --json`). If it is set
and not `implementer` — most commonly a mid-planning gap round that
parked via `fgos ask` inside `fgos-coding-exploring` and was `answer`ed
since — reclaim before continuing:

```bash
fgos handoff-return "<id>" --note "reclaiming at Bootstrap — holder was <role>"
```

Repeat, re-reading `holder` fresh each time, until it reads `implementer`
(a nested call can sit two deep). Stop when a call refuses with "no open
call" — the ordinary end state.

Skip when the item's domain declares no role graph.

## Read the lane

Read the lane `fgos-routing`'s own Orient step already decided for this
item (tiny/small/standard/high-risk/spike, plus the flag count and which
flags applied) — carried into this session as prose, never re-derived
here. Record that same count, those same flags, and the lane into
`plan.md` itself using the literal `Mode: <lane>` label (e.g. `Mode:
tiny` or `mode = **standard**`) — **never rename this recorded label to
`Lane:`**, even though this skill's own prose calls the concept "lane"
now: planning stage's own skip-and-advance short-circuit parses this
exact literal token from `plan.md` to skip a real model call on a
`tiny`/`small` item, and has no idea the concept was ever renamed (a real
regression once broke this coupling across 25 of this repo's own
`plan.md` files matching the old `Mode:` token while a lane recorded as
`Lane:` silently fell through to a real, unnecessary model call). Above
`small`, say plainly why a smaller lane would not honestly cover the
item. This is prose in `plan.md` — never a new field on the item, never a
value `stage` takes.

## Direct-entry fallback

`fgos-coding-exploring` and `fgos-coding-validating` can both hand off
straight into this skill without going through `fgos-routing` first,
which means a lane is not guaranteed to already be sitting in this
session's context. Check, in order:

1. Does `plan.md` already record a `Mode:` line from an earlier round (a
   hand-back from `fgos-coding-validating`, or this same item re-entering
   after a mid-planning CONTEXT.md gap) — if so, that recorded lane IS the
   answer, read it, never re-derive past it.
2. Did this session's own Orient step actually hand off a lane in prose —
   if so, use it, same as always.

Only when NEITHER of those holds — nobody has ever decided a lane for
this item — read and apply `fgos-routing`'s own Mode-gate subsection
directly (point at that source instead of restating its thresholds
inline — an earlier version of this fallback did that and silently
dropped the hard-gate flag enumeration and the tiny/small tie-breaker in
the retelling). This is not the "never re-derive" red flag firing — that
rule guards against overriding a lane already decided by either check
above; this is the one case where nobody decided one yet, and this skill
is genuinely the first to see the item.

1. **Verify Real Commit:** Directly inspect git history in the worktree (`git -C "$wt" log -1 --stat`) to verify substantive changes were committed.
2. **Verify Clean Tree:** Verify `git -C "$wt" status --porcelain` is clean (all worker edits committed).
3. **Execute Verification Directly:** The driver runs the required focused test command directly in the worktree, asserting exit code 0 and all assertions passing.
4. **Caveat Rule:** Caveats reported by reviewer or red-team operations block session completion and require uncaveated re-execution per driver discipline Step 4.

The unit / workflow run schema has no field for a proof tier, `FULL_TRIGGERS`, or an environment fingerprint, and `disposition`/`rationale` accepts any non-empty string regardless of what it claims. A driver who does not actually run `FULL_TEST`, or who mislabels a real regression as `environmental-precondition`, is not caught by anything the runner checks -- this section is entirely Lead discipline in prose, not an enforced gate.

---

## 3. Independent Verification of Doer Commit and Tests

The driver must never accept worker self-narration, conversational claims, or ungrounded status reports:

1. **Verify Real Commit:** Directly inspect git history in the worktree (`git -C "$wt" log -1 --stat`) to verify substantive changes were committed.
2. **Verify Clean Tree:** Verify `git -C "$wt" status --porcelain` is clean (all worker edits committed).

# Named sandbox class (Git spec §13, external-consumer CI): git here touches only the
# fresh repository this function creates under $tmpBase.
function New-Project([string]$Name) {
    $dir = Join-Path $tmpBase $Name
    New-Item -ItemType Directory -Path $dir | Out-Null
    $r = Invoke-Native 'git' @('init', '-q') $dir
    Assert-True ($r.Code -eq 0) "git init in $Name`: $($r.Text)"

  # The repository's common dir, read from the layout Git keeps on disk (no git
  # child; same reading as scripts/lib/git-dir-layout.mjs repositoryDirs): walk
  # up from the physical cwd to the first .git -- a directory is the common dir;
  # a file names "gitdir: <path>" (relative to its directory unless absolute),
  # whose commondir file, when present, names the common dir relative to it.
  # Inlined in each function on purpose: a sourced-shell snapshot drops
  # _-prefixed helpers (tsk-3k2).
  common_dir="" dir=$(pwd -P)
  while :; do
    if [ -d "$dir/.git" ]; then common_dir="$dir/.git"; break; fi
    if [ -f "$dir/.git" ]; then
      git_dir=$(sed -n 's/^gitdir:[[:space:]]*\(.*[^[:space:]]\)[[:space:]]*$/\1/p' "$dir/.git" 2>/dev/null | head -n 1)
      [ -n "$git_dir" ] || break
      case "$git_dir" in /*) ;; *) git_dir="$dir/$git_dir" ;; esac
      common_dir="$git_dir"
      if [ -f "$git_dir/commondir" ]; then
        common_dir=$(head -n 1 "$git_dir/commondir")
        case "$common_dir" in /*) ;; *) common_dir="$git_dir/$common_dir" ;; esac

    fi

    return 1
  fi

* The CLI door's queue. The full-suite queue is a kernel lock taken through the
 * in-process door of the native addon, and this process runs from a checkout,
 * whose door loads only through the one staged manifest: so the checkout's addon
 * and host are staged (one cargo build per run, here, never per selected file)
 * and exported on this process's env before the lock is asked for. Staging
 * outside the queue is safe: it builds into this run's own CARGO_TARGET_DIR (cargo
 * serializes a shared one) and publishes into this checkout's own staging directory
 * by atomic rename, so a run queued in another worktree never executes bytes
 * replaced under it. What stays inside the queue is the heavy work: the release
 * artifacts and the suite itself.
 */

 * carries a running mark for a different file, and only then writes its proof

 * nothing outside its worktree; the item's log keeps it). Under sequential
 * dispatch the first worker never sees a peer: it writes nothing, fails
 * goal-check and the item parks. No wall-clock bound decides the outcome, so
 * a slow machine only makes the wait longer, never the proof weaker. */

2494abb515045bed4abdddeef71903fae5d0beb3.boundText: - `bin/fgos.mjs` — CLI một cửa của work-state; chạy `node bin/fgos.mjs <verb>`; gồm verb `edit` — sửa đè các trường (title/kind/risk/verify/tier/refs/deps/acceptance/priority/intent — str7-str8-priority-intent) trên một item đã có, cùng cửa ghi CTR002 như `add`/`move`; gồm verb `take`/`return` — cửa pull giao–nhận việc cho tác nhân ngoài runner; gồm verb `pick` — cửa pull GỘP `take` + dựng workspace (`createWorktree`), role cố định `session`, không cờ `--role` (theo str83-fgos-slash-commands); gồm verb `review`/`approve`/`reject` — cổng duyệt PR nội bộ, một cổng cho mọi đề xuất `awaiting-approval`, nay leaf-vs-root-aware (con nhập vào nhánh của gốc, gốc nhập vào cây chính); `review`/`approve` nay chấp nhận thêm `--github [--pr <n>]` — vận chuyển thay thế CÙNG cổng duyệt qua GitHub thay vì diff/merge cục bộ (chỉ nguồn runner, theo github-adapter, spec: docs/specs/runner.md); gồm verb `catchup` — đồng bộ lại một việc đỗ vì gãy nhập/trôi tích hợp (spec: docs/specs/runner.md); gồm verb `session` (`start`/`end`/`list`) — vòng đời phiên checkout đa-phiên tùy chọn, mỗi phiên một worktree detached-HEAD cho cây nguồn, dùng chung MỘT kho `.fgos/` qua symlink (spec: docs/specs/runner.md); spec: docs/specs/work-state.md

ec87bb4aa1a43d0b817713ada0181e472cbda6f4.boundText: - `src/state/` — lõi work-state: events (nhật ký; `appendEvent` nay chạy trong mutex nóng `state` (`withStateTx`, `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`) — xem spec Work-State RUL10 (tiền đề có ngưỡng — một người ghi tại một thời điểm; multi-agent ghi đồng thời qua mutex nóng `state`)), work (schema — STATUSES + STAGES + field `parent` lineage + field `domain`), fsm (bảng chuyển status + CAS), stage (bảng chuyển stage + CAS, chiều vĩ mô song song fsm; cạnh chuyển-stage tra theo domain của item — `coding`: `discovery → exploring → planning → executing`, trong đó phán-quyết `clear` ở `discovery` bỏ qua `exploring` để sang thẳng `planning` còn `unclear` đi qua `exploring`; tên `decompose` vẫn còn nhưng chỉ là bí danh legacy chỉ-để-rút-cạn (không việc MỚI nào vào được nữa); `synthetic`: một stage, không cạnh nào), domains (sổ đăng ký domain — stage list + step-mapping base-workflow + cạnh-chuyển mỗi domain; `coding` + ba domain minh họa/thử-nghiệm `synthetic` (đúng một stage), `triage`, `fixture-marketing`; base-workflow-model STR18, hoàn tất S1+S2), replay (fold), frontier (truy vấn sẵn-sàng — lọc theo status, stage domain-aware, VÀ lineage qua `parent`), dep-graph (dò chu trình trên `deps` — bất biến phi-chu-trình tại cửa ghi, per work-graph-intelligence S1), store (chủ ghi duy nhất + readRawEvents), envelope (phong bì output CTR001, `wrapEnvelope` — nay bọc MỌI verb ở một cửa in trong `bin/fgos.mjs main()`, STR37; spec: docs/specs/work-state.md §envelope)

9be1b9579691d32e5a15d299bae390dfcc531b95.boundText: - `domains/coding/AGENTS.md` `## fgOS Workflow` + `.claude/skills/` (`.agents/skills/` mirror byte-identical) — lớp hướng dẫn P50: entry skill (`fgos-routing`) + skill giai đoạn (`fgos-coding-discovering`/`fgos-coding-exploring`/`fgos-coding-planning`/`fgos-coding-validating`/`fgos-coding-implement`/`fgos-coding-knowledge`) trỏ một phiên tự mở tới đúng skill theo `stage` của item; từ str89-fgos-domain-skills, tra cứu này domain-pluggable — đọc trường `domain` + `stage` của item rồi tra qua `skillForStage`/`getDomain` (`src/state/workflow-stage-graphs.mjs`), không còn giả định ngầm domain `coding`; `fgos-routing` nay có hàng khoá theo **status** `retrospective → fgos-coding-knowledge` (skill tổng hợp cấp nhãn Diataxis + soạn tài liệu người-dùng-cuối) — stage `compound-learn` đã rút, việc tổng hợp nó từng canh nay là việc của status `retrospective`; skill ĐỘC LẬP `fgos-submit-assist` (str51-llm-assist-classify) đã rút (tsk-6ar) — `/fgOS:submit` bước 6 (`plugins/fgOS/skills/submit/SKILL.md`) nay tự chạy clarify+classify trong cùng phiên sống, cùng việc mà skill đó từng làm nhưng trên bản mô tả SẠCH hơn; spec: docs/specs/work-state.md §RUL60 (hành vi), docs/specs/runner.md (lớp hướng dẫn)

a69b84a28979f1ba4e1f114d7e795824fcfc69c1.boundText: - `src/runner/` + `bin/fgos-runner.mjs` — vòng tự hành (loop/dispatch/worktree/recovery/anti-loop/write-queue/root-affinity); `loop.mjs`'s `runWatch` + `write-queue.mjs`'s `onCommit` — chế độ `--watch` bền, tín hiệu-cơ-học + nghỉ dự phòng, ghép `runOnce` không đổi làm hộp đen (str7-str8-priority-intent, spec: docs/specs/runner.md §RUL53 (`--watch` — vòng cầm-giao bền, dừng chỉ khi có tín hiệu tường minh)); loop giao việc theo mẻ song song có giới hạn hai tầng (cấu hình `parallel` trong `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner` section, theo tsk-5vf), giữ quyền-sở-hữu-gốc trong một lượt chạy, quét làm-rõ rồi quét chia-việc trước mọi dispatch thi công; gặt-lại bỏ qua claim của cửa pull (`claimRole` human/session); `dispatch.mjs`'s executor là port có tên CTR009 v2 (`EXECUTOR_ADAPTERS`, per-tier qua config's `executors`, STR41), `ensureRunnerConfigForDir` tự sinh cấu hình mặc định tại `.fgos/config.json` khi vắng mặt (không áp dụng cho `--config` tường minh, str76-runner-bootstrap; tsk-5hv xoá hẳn fallback về file flat legacy cũ); worker của loop và fan-out chạy như một Unit run qua `runUnit` (`work-dispatch.mjs`'s `spawnWorker`), `fgos-runner` không còn `--config` (spec: docs/specs/runner.md §RUL93 (the runner loop's worker and the fan-out batch run as one Unit run each)) và prompt worker được tách sang `prompt-templates.mjs` + `prompt-templates/*.txt` (chọn template qua bảng cơ học kind/tier/domain, substitution `{placeholder}` thuần, log dispatch kèm tên+hash template, STR49); `goal-check.mjs` — hàm goal-check dùng chung giữa vòng tự hành và verb `return`; `write-queue.mjs` — cửa ghi tuần tự giữ một-người-ghi dưới song song; `root-affinity.mjs` — quyền-sở-hữu-gốc, giữ mọi con của một gốc chung một chủ trong một lượt chạy; `resolveRepoRoot` nay còn xác nhận HEAD repo resolve được trước khi runner claim bất kỳ item nào (fail-fast, str86-runner-headless-git D ecfd0d1a); config: `.fgos/config.json`'s `runner` section (tự sinh khi vắng mặt tại đường mặc định, nguồn config duy nhất kể từ tsk-5hv); spec: docs/specs/runner.md

1c1c0d7820346c21fcecad8a1dae2911ed126632.boundText: | Work Lifecycle Engine / Work Driver | Domain-agnostic work-unit lifecycle, status board, claim/return, human gates. Does not own stage or sequencing (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): execution and progress authority for a case on the ledger is the Workflow case, and Work keeps the status lifecycle, claim/return, slots, settlement and the `workflowRunId` pointer; the coding step FSM stays the authority for coding items until the coding cutover. Owns worker slots (`OccupancyPort`), and fail-safe claim settlement (`fgos return --to blocked`). | [../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md](../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md) |
1c1c0d7820346c21fcecad8a1dae2911ed126632.currentText:
| Work Lifecycle Engine / Work Driver | Domain-agnostic work-unit lifecycle, status board, claim/return, human gates. Does not own stage or sequencing (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md)): execution and progress authority for a case on the ledger is the Workflow case, and Work keeps the status lifecycle, claim/return, slots, settlement and the `workflowRunId` pointer; the coding step FSM stays the authority for coding items until the coding cutover. Owns worker slots (`OccupancyPort`), and fail-safe claim settlement (`fgos return --to blocked`). | [../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md](../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md) |
| Workflow (guide + case; `src/workflow/**`) | Component Workflow with two entities, guide and case (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), partially supersedes 0048 §2 and 0049 §4; behaviour per [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md), implementation follows its plan). Human review gates. A consumer of Git's Land and Sync; owns no git mutation of its own. Single authority for the guide schema and its pinned snapshot per case; the case ledger (approved frame, reservations, route/deviation events, gate answers bound to subject digests, receipts, milestone projection, close); admission (is a proposed activity lawful now, against a closed catalog of machine checks); the worktree binding record (keyed by worktree root identity, with a generation) and the frame counters. Implements the AdmissionPort that Execution Core declares; imports flow Workflow → Execution Core only. Chooses no order: the agent proposes, the case admits and records; the Playbook proposer proposes through admission like any agent. Admission predicates, projection and the port implementation sit at infra or lower; the Playbook proposer at use-case. The ledger stays the JSONL under `advance`, hardened in place (fsync before release, reader fails closed); not an Event Store consumer in this cutover (owner 2026-10-19). Consumer of Execution Core and Git. Never owns who/model/persona, verify execution, locks, writer identity, merge or Work status. | [workflow/spec.md](workflow/spec.md), [runner/spec.md](runner/spec.md) |
| Execution Core (Unit, Unit run, `bind()`, Pattern cộng tác, cửa `fgos run`, posture) | Single authority for how a Unit runs (mechanism, posture, gates), through a single run door for new work (`fgos run` via `src/runner/execution/run.mjs`, herdr pane default, cli fallback), OS confinement posture for both herdr and cli, verifiable mutating gate. Strictly forbids L3 Work lifecycle dependencies (`src/state/**`). Owns the AdmissionPort interface (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md)) (resolve the target worktree's binding, admit, settle), never the admission decision; every `runUnit` caller with writes (the run door, the Playbook proposer and the Work paths running today) injects Workflow's real implementation from the day it lands, and the port accepts an `advance` hold the caller already has. `runUnit` refuses a mutating Unit with no port, and a standalone write passes only on an affirmative `unbound`. The door resolves the caller's authority context conjunctively after pattern resolution and before `bind()`; the port stays present at the mutating gate, which re-checks subject-bound consent at effect; the door sets the case context in the worker's launch env and strips any inherited one. A nested writing dispatch from a confined worker is refused by name (owner 2026-10-19). It no longer chooses a seat: which executor, model, effort, tier and account an agent seat gets, and where it goes on failure, belongs to Seat Binding (next row, D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding)); `src/runner/execution/bind.mjs` is the thin facade that collects machine facts and asks it. Persona files are loaded by `agent-definitions` (names and paths by Convention). | [runner/spec.md](runner/spec.md) |
| Seat Binding (`fgos-seat-binding`) | Single authority for "which executor, invocation, model, effort, tier and account runs this agent seat, and where it goes on failure", with the reason for each part ([spec §3](seat-binding/spec.md)). Two pure stages in a Rust crate (static policy, then ranking) behind the internal route `fgos internal seat-binding bind\|ladder`; thin Node client `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` (fails closed; inside an activated release the activation host answers). Depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. Agent seats only: a capability served by a tool executor keeps its own path. Account state (lease, release, quarantine, probe) is reached through the provider-capacity port: the facade reads the account view outside the provider lock, and the lease takes exactly the account the crate named; no host exec runs under that lock. Owns the tier ladder (the source of the config `$comment`). Does not own the seat list (the seat resolver, from pattern and workflow `seats:`), launching, transport, confinement, admission or persona loading. | [seat-binding/spec.md](seat-binding/spec.md), `packages/seat-binding/rust`, `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` |
| Collaboration Patterns (Execution Core) | Domain-neutral small collaboration loops (`solo`, `reviewed`, `panel`) and presets (`consult`, `research-fan-out`, `rfc`). Replaces retired coordination engine. | [runner/spec.md](runner/spec.md) |
| Herdr (Transport chính + Bề mặt quan sát) | Transport mặc định cho out-of-process runs, pane execution liveness, plugin `herdr-dashboard/` (TUI trong pane herdr + pick/pane supervisor; herdr nạp qua `herdr-plugin.toml`). | [herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md](herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md) |
| fgos Gateway | Tiến trình detached duy nhất phục vụ REST API (`/v1`, hợp đồng CTR010), MCP `search`/`execute` trên cùng cổng, và bundle web dashboard nhúng sẵn (`apps/fgos-gateway/`: `gateway.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `cf_access.rs`, `remote_invocation.rs`, `web/`). Vòng đời duy nhất qua `fgos gateway start\|status\|stop`; không phải một phần của herdr và không phải "herdr-gateway" (tên đó chỉ repo tham chiếu ngoài). Dùng chung với `herdr-dashboard` lớp adapter CLI fgos tại `packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust` (`fgos.rs`, `settings.rs`, trait `WorkItemSource`). | [herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md](herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md) |
| Dispatch Transport & Confinement | Machine backend registry, isolation confinement (`bwrap` v1 driver, attestation storage, fail-closed probes), executor adapters; the `bwrap` driver calls the credential renewal module at provisioning (`copyCredentialFiles`, the write-back marker) and removing a private home (`confinement/cleanup.mjs`) calls it again for write-back (dependency confinement → provider capacity, for the account lock only). | [agent-confinement/spec.md](agent-confinement/spec.md) |

| Work Lifecycle Engine / Work Driver | Domain-agnostic work-unit lifecycle, status board, claim/return, human gates. Does not own stage or sequencing (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md)): execution and progress authority for a case on the ledger is the Workflow case, and Work keeps the status lifecycle, claim/return, slots, settlement and the `workflowRunId` pointer; the coding step FSM stays the authority for coding items until the coding cutover. Owns worker slots (`OccupancyPort`), and fail-safe claim settlement (`fgos return --to blocked`). | [../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md](../architect/component-boundary/component-boundary-advisory.md) |
| Workflow (guide + case; `src/workflow/**`) | Component Workflow with two entities, guide and case (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), partially supersedes 0048 §2 and 0049 §4; behaviour per [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md), implementation follows its plan). Human review gates. A consumer of Git's Land and Sync; owns no git mutation of its own. Single authority for the guide schema and its pinned snapshot per case; the case ledger (approved frame, reservations, route/deviation events, gate answers bound to subject digests, receipts, milestone projection, close); admission (is a proposed activity lawful now, against a closed catalog of machine checks); the worktree binding record (keyed by worktree root identity, with a generation) and the frame counters. Implements the AdmissionPort that Execution Core declares; imports flow Workflow → Execution Core only. Chooses no order: the agent proposes, the case admits and records; the Playbook proposer proposes through admission like any agent. Admission predicates, projection and the port implementation sit at infra or lower; the Playbook proposer at use-case. The ledger stays the JSONL under `advance`, hardened in place (fsync before release, reader fails closed); not an Event Store consumer in this cutover (owner 2026-10-19). Consumer of Execution Core and Git. Never owns who/model/persona, verify execution, locks, writer identity, merge or Work status. | [workflow/spec.md](workflow/spec.md), [runner/spec.md](runner/spec.md) |
| Execution Core (Unit, Unit run, `bind()`, Pattern cộng tác, cửa `fgos run`, posture) | Single authority for how a Unit runs (mechanism, posture, gates), through a single run door for new work (`fgos run` via `src/runner/execution/run.mjs`, herdr pane default, cli fallback), OS confinement posture for both herdr and cli, verifiable mutating gate. Strictly forbids L3 Work lifecycle dependencies (`src/state/**`). Owns the AdmissionPort interface (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), [workflow.md](workflow/spec.md)) (resolve the target worktree's binding, admit, settle), never the admission decision; every `runUnit` caller with writes (the run door, the Playbook proposer and the Work paths running today) injects Workflow's real implementation from the day it lands, and the port accepts an `advance` hold the caller already has. `runUnit` refuses a mutating Unit with no port, and a standalone write passes only on an affirmative `unbound`. The door resolves the caller's authority context conjunctively after pattern resolution and before `bind()`; the port stays present at the mutating gate, which re-checks subject-bound consent at effect; the door sets the case context in the worker's launch env and strips any inherited one. A nested writing dispatch from a confined worker is refused by name (owner 2026-10-19). It no longer chooses a seat: which executor, model, effort, tier and account an agent seat gets, and where it goes on failure, belongs to Seat Binding (next row, D-ADR0072 (Seat Binding)); `src/runner/execution/bind.mjs` is the thin facade that collects machine facts and asks it. Persona files are loaded by `agent-definitions` (names and paths by Convention). | [runner/spec.md](runner/spec.md) |
| Seat Binding (`fgos-seat-binding`) | Single authority for "which executor, invocation, model, effort, tier and account runs this agent seat, and where it goes on failure", with the reason for each part ([spec §3](seat-binding/spec.md)). Two pure stages in a Rust crate (static policy, then ranking) behind the internal route `fgos internal seat-binding bind\|ladder`; thin Node client `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` (fails closed; inside an activated release the activation host answers). Depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. Agent seats only: a capability served by a tool executor keeps its own path. Account state (lease, release, quarantine, probe) is reached through the provider-capacity port: the facade reads the account view outside the provider lock, and the lease takes exactly the account the crate named; no host exec runs under that lock. Owns the tier ladder (the source of the config `$comment`). Does not own the seat list (the seat resolver, from pattern and workflow `seats:`), launching, transport, confinement, admission or persona loading. | [seat-binding/spec.md](seat-binding/spec.md), `packages/seat-binding/rust`, `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` |

| Seat Binding (`fgos-seat-binding`) | Single authority for "which executor, invocation, model, effort, tier and account runs this agent seat, and where it goes on failure", with the reason for each part ([spec §3](seat-binding/spec.md)). Two pure stages in a Rust crate (static policy, then ranking) behind the internal route `fgos internal seat-binding bind\|ladder`; thin Node client `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` (fails closed; inside an activated release the activation host answers). Depends only on `fgos-host-runtime`. Agent seats only: a capability served by a tool executor keeps its own path. Account state (lease, release, quarantine, probe) is reached through the provider-capacity port: the facade reads the account view outside the provider lock, and the lease takes exactly the account the crate named; no host exec runs under that lock. Owns the tier ladder (the source of the config `$comment`). Does not own the seat list (the seat resolver, from pattern and workflow `seats:`), launching, transport, confinement, admission or persona loading. | [seat-binding/spec.md](seat-binding/spec.md), `packages/seat-binding/rust`, `src/seat-binding/client.mjs` |
| Collaboration Patterns (Execution Core) | Domain-neutral small collaboration loops (`solo`, `reviewed`, `panel`) and presets (`consult`, `research-fan-out`, `rfc`). Replaces retired coordination engine. | [runner/spec.md](runner/spec.md) |
| Herdr (Transport chính + Bề mặt quan sát) | Transport mặc định cho out-of-process runs, pane execution liveness, plugin `herdr-dashboard/` (TUI trong pane herdr + pick/pane supervisor; herdr nạp qua `herdr-plugin.toml`). | [herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md](herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md) |
| fgos Gateway | Tiến trình detached duy nhất phục vụ REST API (`/v1`, hợp đồng CTR010), MCP `search`/`execute` trên cùng cổng, và bundle web dashboard nhúng sẵn (`apps/fgos-gateway/`: `gateway.rs`, `mcp.rs`, `cf_access.rs`, `remote_invocation.rs`, `web/`). Vòng đời duy nhất qua `fgos gateway start\|status\|stop`; không phải một phần của herdr và không phải "herdr-gateway" (tên đó chỉ repo tham chiếu ngoài). Dùng chung với `herdr-dashboard` lớp adapter CLI fgos tại `packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust` (`fgos.rs`, `settings.rs`, trait `WorkItemSource`). | [herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md](herdr-web-dashboard/spec.md) |
| Dispatch Transport & Confinement | Machine backend registry, isolation confinement (`bwrap` v1 driver, attestation storage, fail-closed probes), executor adapters; the `bwrap` driver calls the credential renewal module at provisioning (`copyCredentialFiles`, the write-back marker) and removing a private home (`confinement/cleanup.mjs`) calls it again for write-back (dependency confinement → provider capacity, for the account lock only). | [agent-confinement/spec.md](agent-confinement/spec.md) |

2679aaa826ac9e735c3d6be5b5c5f035e837c562.boundText: | Holder-lock (L1) | Single authority for "who holds which resource", as the kernel sees it: kernel locks on open file descriptions behind one OS-neutral port (`acquire`, `release`, `run_borrowed`, `probe`, `holders`, `guarantee`), the lock registry (`packages/holder-lock/contracts/lock-registry.v1.json`: every lock's kind, scope, rank, path, legacy shape and fence), lock order inside one `LockScope`, the description rules, the predecessor-domain rule, the single state-root resolution and the cutover fences. Never reads writer identity, never takes a lock from a live holder, never derives a decision from a pid, TTL or mtime. Rust crate `fgos-holder-lock` (`packages/holder-lock/rust`) plus the internal routes `fgos internal lock-fd|state-root|quiesce-scan|lock-borrow-vectors`; Node only through the facade `src/holder-lock/`, which never exposes an fd. Depends on Process Facts & Control and the kernel. Owns the cold locks (gateway, runner, sessions, advance, reconcile, recovery, full-suite, provider account/state, dispatch cwd) and the main checkout mutex (one door `withMainCheckout`, git children and the pre-commit hook borrow the lock through the description, no pid or TTL), the merge slot and `worktree-admin`; `fgos lock fence` is the one door for a hung live holder. `advance` follows Shape C (D-ADR0070 (workflow guide + admission ledger), owner 2026-10-19, [workflow.md](../specs/workflow.md)): a conductor case holds it for one reserve or one release/settle; the Playbook proposer holds it for the life of its loop, so its holder is the proposer's liveness, as today; a dispatch naming a live playbook case from inside its own Unit is refused by name. `answer` never appends directly: it writes the gate-answer file and tries `advance` once. The worktree binding is one exclusively created file per worktree, not a registry row. No new lock row; rank stays 80; no re-rank for an Event Store cutover. It does not own the state store's hot mutex (`state`, `porting-events`: `withStateTx` in `src/state/hot-lock.mjs`, which replaced `events.lock`, `claims.lock` and `porting/events.lock`): the state store owns that mechanism, a temporary one until the store moves to Rust, and takes only its cleanup lock and the fences from this component. The main door's `.fgos` checkpoint is a detachable adapter, so the lock core knows nothing of the event log. | [holder-lock/spec.md](holder-lock/spec.md) |
