[package]
name = "fgos-gateway"
version = "0.2.0"
edition = "2021"

[lib]
name = "fgos_gateway"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "fgos-gateway"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0"
# tsk-7l9-2 D8: fgos-gateway's first async dependency -- the gateway's REST
# surface (D1/D7) is what needs one; the TUI/orchestrator code stays fully
# synchronous and untouched.
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "process", "net", "time", "fs"] }
# tsk-7l9-3: bumped 0.7 -> 0.8 -- required by `rmcp`'s streamable-http-server
# transport (mcp.rs), which only supports axum ^0.8. Breaking route-syntax
# change (`:id` -> `{id}`) rewritten across every existing route in
# gateway.rs's `build_router`; no other breaking change touches this crate
# (State/middleware::from_fn_with_state/Json extraction are unaffected).
axum = "0.8"
# tsk-7l9-3 D1: MCP surface's server SDK -- the official
# modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk, tokio-async, mounts its
# `transport::streamable_http_server::StreamableHttpService` directly onto an
# existing `axum::Router` via `.nest_service()` (confirmed against the SDK's
# own `examples/servers/src/counter_streamhttp.rs`), so `search`/`execute`
# ride the SAME router/port `tsk-7l9-2`'s REST surface already serves -- no
# second process, no second listener. `mcpkit-axum` (this plan's original
# pick alongside rmcp) turned out to be a wholly separate, non-composable MCP
# SDK (`mcpkit-core`/`mcpkit-server`/`mcpkit-transport`, unrelated to rmcp) --
# dropped, rmcp alone covers the whole surface.
rmcp = { version = "3", features = ["server", "macros", "transport-streamable-http-server", "schemars"] }
# tsk-7l9-3 D1: `execute`'s bound-function scripting language (Approach's own
# rhai-over-mlua pick: pure Rust, no vendored-C/system-Lua dependency, matches
# D1's "no extra runtime layer" rationale). `serde` feature turns bound
# function results (serde_json::Value) into Rhai `Dynamic` values and back.
rhai = { version = "1", features = ["serde"] }
# tsk-7l9-3: `search`'s only new data need -- parses the OpenAPI contract
# (`docs/contracts/fgos-gateway-api-v1.yaml`) into a queryable operation list
# instead of serving it as an opaque string the way `/contract` already does.
serde_yaml = "0.9"
# tsk-54y: CORS layer for `build_router` -- the web client (a separate
# static bundle, D2 of docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard-plan-realignment/
# CONTEXT.md) is not guaranteed to share origin with the gateway. Version
# resolved by `cargo add --dry-run` against this crate's existing axum 0.8
# dependency graph (docs/history/tsk-54y-gateway-cors-bind/plan.md).
tower-http = { version = "0.7", features = ["cors", "fs"] }
# tsk-48w (D14 of docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard-plan-realignment/
# CONTEXT.md): embeds apps/fgos-gateway/web's built bundle into the binary so
# the "máy được chọn" can serve it with no separate deploy step.
# Versions resolved by real `cargo add --dry-run` against this crate's
# existing dependency graph (docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard/plan.md,
# "NẮN LẠI P1 tsk-48w"): rust-embed 8.12.0, axum-embed 0.1.0, same
# rust-embed major line the reference implementation herdr-gateway pins.
rust-embed = { version = "8", features = ["debug-embed"] }
axum-embed = "0.1"
# tsk-6arn (D8): Cloudflare Access as auth layer 2, additive to the
# Bearer token layer already shipped (tsk-7l9). Ported from the reference
# implementation herdr-gateway (crate herdr-go, src/web/cf_access.rs).
# Versions resolved by real `cargo add --dry-run` against this crate's
# existing dependency graph -- differ from the reference's own pins
# (jsonwebtoken 9->11, reqwest 0.12->0.13; reqwest's TLS feature was
# renamed `rustls-tls`->`rustls` between those versions, confirmed by a
# real dry-run failure before the correction). `jsonwebtoken`'s
# `aws_lc_rs` feature is required explicitly -- v11 ships neither crypto
# backend by default (real runtime panic caught at Execute: "Could not
# automatically determine the process-level CryptoProvider... make sure
# exactly one of the 'rust_crypto' and 'aws_lc_rs' features is enabled"),
# and `aws_lc_rs` matches the backend `reqwest`'s own `rustls` feature
# already pulls in, avoiding a second, competing provider in the same
# binary.
jsonwebtoken = { version = "11", default-features = false, features = ["use_pem", "aws_lc_rs"] }
reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["json", "rustls"] }
base64 = "0.23"
herdr-fgos-common = { path = "../../packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust" }
fgos-host-runtime = { path = "../../packages/host-runtime/rust" }
fgos-distribution = { path = "../../packages/distribution/rust" }

[dev-dependencies]
tower = { version = "0.4", features = ["util"] }

# tsk-7l9-2 D8: fgos-gateway's first async dependency -- the gateway's REST
# surface (D1/D7) is what needs one; the TUI/orchestrator code stays fully
# synchronous and untouched.
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "process", "net", "time", "fs"] }
# tsk-7l9-3: bumped 0.7 -> 0.8 -- required by `rmcp`'s streamable-http-server
# transport (mcp.rs), which only supports axum ^0.8. Breaking route-syntax
# change (`:id` -> `{id}`) rewritten across every existing route in
# gateway.rs's `build_router`; no other breaking change touches this crate
# (State/middleware::from_fn_with_state/Json extraction are unaffected).
axum = "0.8"
# tsk-7l9-3 D1: MCP surface's server SDK -- the official
# modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk, tokio-async, mounts its
# `transport::streamable_http_server::StreamableHttpService` directly onto an
# existing `axum::Router` via `.nest_service()` (confirmed against the SDK's
# own `examples/servers/src/counter_streamhttp.rs`), so `search`/`execute`
# ride the SAME router/port `tsk-7l9-2`'s REST surface already serves -- no
# second process, no second listener. `mcpkit-axum` (this plan's original
# pick alongside rmcp) turned out to be a wholly separate, non-composable MCP
# SDK (`mcpkit-core`/`mcpkit-server`/`mcpkit-transport`, unrelated to rmcp) --
# dropped, rmcp alone covers the whole surface.
rmcp = { version = "3", features = ["server", "macros", "transport-streamable-http-server", "schemars"] }
# tsk-7l9-3 D1: `execute`'s bound-function scripting language (Approach's own
# rhai-over-mlua pick: pure Rust, no vendored-C/system-Lua dependency, matches
# D1's "no extra runtime layer" rationale). `serde` feature turns bound
# function results (serde_json::Value) into Rhai `Dynamic` values and back.
rhai = { version = "1", features = ["serde"] }
# tsk-7l9-3: `search`'s only new data need -- parses the OpenAPI contract
# (`docs/contracts/fgos-gateway-api-v1.yaml`) into a queryable operation list
# instead of serving it as an opaque string the way `/contract` already does.
fgos-yaml-doc = { path = "../../packages/yaml-doc/rust" }
# tsk-54y: CORS layer for `build_router` -- the web client (a separate
# static bundle, D2 of docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard-plan-realignment/
# CONTEXT.md) is not guaranteed to share origin with the gateway. Version
# resolved by `cargo add --dry-run` against this crate's existing axum 0.8
# dependency graph (docs/history/tsk-54y-gateway-cors-bind/plan.md).
tower-http = { version = "0.7", features = ["cors", "fs"] }
# tsk-48w (D14 of docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard-plan-realignment/
# CONTEXT.md): embeds apps/fgos-gateway/web's built bundle into the binary so
# the "máy được chọn" can serve it with no separate deploy step.
# Versions resolved by real `cargo add --dry-run` against this crate's
# existing dependency graph (docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard/plan.md,
# "NẮN LẠI P1 tsk-48w"): rust-embed 8.12.0, axum-embed 0.1.0, same
# rust-embed major line the reference implementation herdr-gateway pins.
rust-embed = { version = "8", features = ["debug-embed"] }
axum-embed = "0.1"
# tsk-6arn (D8): Cloudflare Access as auth layer 2, additive to the
# Bearer token layer already shipped (tsk-7l9). Ported from the reference
# implementation herdr-gateway (crate herdr-go, src/web/cf_access.rs).
# Versions resolved by real `cargo add --dry-run` against this crate's
# existing dependency graph -- differ from the reference's own pins
# (jsonwebtoken 9->11, reqwest 0.12->0.13; reqwest's TLS feature was
# renamed `rustls-tls`->`rustls` between those versions, confirmed by a
# real dry-run failure before the correction). `jsonwebtoken`'s
# `aws_lc_rs` feature is required explicitly -- v11 ships neither crypto
# backend by default (real runtime panic caught at Execute: "Could not
# automatically determine the process-level CryptoProvider... make sure
# exactly one of the 'rust_crypto' and 'aws_lc_rs' features is enabled"),
# and `aws_lc_rs` matches the backend `reqwest`'s own `rustls` feature
# already pulls in, avoiding a second, competing provider in the same
# binary.
jsonwebtoken = { version = "11", default-features = false, features = ["use_pem", "aws_lc_rs"] }
reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["json", "rustls"] }
base64 = "0.23"
herdr-fgos-common = { path = "../../packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust" }
fgos-host-runtime = { path = "../../packages/host-runtime/rust" }
fgos-distribution = { path = "../../packages/distribution/rust" }
fgos-git = { path = "../../packages/git/rust" }

[dev-dependencies]
tower = { version = "0.4", features = ["util"] }

# fgos-yaml-doc pins its parser to the vendored copies under packages/yaml-doc/third-party; this crate
# is outside the root workspace and has its own lock, so it repeats the root [patch.crates-io].
[patch.crates-io]
saphyr-parser = { path = "../../packages/yaml-doc/third-party/saphyr-parser-0.2.2" }
arraydeque = { path = "../../packages/yaml-doc/third-party/arraydeque-0.5.1" }

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# fgOS terminal rename -- best-effort herdr pane label, through the
# terminal-control port (attach, then label). Chrome-only (D2,
# docs/history/fgos-terminal-pane-rename/CONTEXT.md): never touches .fgos/
# state, never blocks the caller. Any missing precondition -- including the
# pane-labeling capability not being registered at all -- is a silent no-op,
# exit 0.
#
# Usage: rename.sh <task-id> <project-root>
#   <task-id>      the claimed fgOS item id (first label segment)
#   <project-root> absolute path to this repo's checkout, so the fgOS
#                  session-id fallback (fg.ssid) can be resolved even when
#                  this script itself runs from an installed plugin cache
#                  copy that doesn't carry src/ alongside it.
set -u

task_id="${1:-}"
project_root="${2:-}"

[ -n "$task_id" ] || exit 0

# Capability gate (D5, docs/history/orchestrator-worker-slots/DISCUSSION.md
# §6 "Nhãn: session tự đặt qua helper skill có gate"). Pane labeling is an
# adapter-swappable capability declared through the tool registry:
#
#   fgos tool register --name herdr --kind cli --capability pane-labeling \
#     --command herdr
#
# Zero registered providers means this environment has no pane-label concept
# at all, so labeling is skipped silently -- the same shape this script
# already had outside a herdr pane, never a failure ("absent capability =
# clean skip", src/state/tool-registry.mjs's own header). Swapping herdr for
# tmux/cmux later means registering a different provider here, not editing
# every caller: this query is the hexagon seam, and it sits ahead of the
# herdr-specific guards below precisely so those guards read as one
# adapter's implementation detail rather than as the gate itself.
#
# Gated on REGISTERED, not on `--status present`: `present` only becomes true
# once someone has run `fgos tool check` on this machine (bin/fgos.mjs's
# `tool query`, resolvedStatus), so gating on it would switch labeling off on
# every fresh clone with no signal. The registry answers "does this
# environment have the concept"; the adapter guards below answer "and is it
# usable right now", which for herdr is a strictly sharper question than a
# PATH probe -- herdr being installed says nothing about this session running
# inside one of its panes.
#
# Any failure to answer the question at all -- no <project-root>, no
# .fgos/installation/bin/fgos or bin/fgos.mjs there, node missing, CLI error --
# falls through to the same no-op. Fail-closed is the right direction for
# decoration: a helper that cannot confirm the capability must not guess
# that it is present.
[ -n "$project_root" ] || exit 0
if [ -x "$project_root/.fgos/installation/bin/fgos" ]; then
  "$project_root/.fgos/installation/bin/fgos" tool query --capability pane-labeling --dir "$project_root" 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -q '"capability" *: *"pane-labeling"' || exit 0
elif [ -f "$project_root/bin/fgos.mjs" ]; then
  node "$project_root/bin/fgos.mjs" tool query --capability pane-labeling --dir "$project_root" 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -q '"capability" *: *"pane-labeling"' || exit 0
else
  exit 0
fi

# herdr adapter -- today's only pane-labeling provider. Not in a
# herdr-managed pane, or herdr unavailable: no-op.
[ "${HERDR_ENV:-}" = "1" ] || exit 0
command -v herdr >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
command -v fgos >/dev/null 2>&1 || exit 0
[ -n "${HERDR_PANE_ID:-}" ] || exit 0
# HERDR_PANE_ID can be inherited from a shared agent daemon and name a dead
# pane or another session's pane: act only on this caller's own live pane.
. "$(dirname "$0")/pane-owned.sh"
. "$(dirname "$0")/terminal-port.sh"
fgos_pane_owned "$HERDR_PANE_ID" || exit 0

# fg.ssid (D1): fgOS's own session id. FGOS_SESSION_ID first, else
# resolveWriterIdentity()'s own env/registry/pid fallback chain
# (src/util/session-identity.mjs) -- dropped entirely if neither resolves.
fg_ssid="${FGOS_SESSION_ID:-}"
if [ -z "$fg_ssid" ] && [ -n "$project_root" ] && [ -f "$project_root/src/util/session-identity.mjs" ]; then
  fg_ssid=$(node -e "
    import(process.argv[1]).then(({ resolveWriterIdentity }) => {
      process.stdout.write(String(resolveWriterIdentity().id));
    }).catch(() => {});
  " -- "$project_root/src/util/session-identity.mjs" 2>/dev/null || true)
fi

# a.ssid (D1): the coding agent tool's own native session id. Claude Code
# exposes CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID; other agent tools are not detected today
# (docs/history/fgos-terminal-pane-rename/CONTEXT.md, outstanding questions)
# and simply drop this segment (D4).
a_ssid="${CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID:-}"

# resolveWriterIdentity()'s own fallback chain reads CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ID
# too when FGOS_SESSION_ID is unset, so fg_ssid can come back equal to
# a_ssid -- collapsing the two genuinely-distinct identities D1 requires.
# Drop the duplicate rather than show the same value twice.
if [ -n "$fg_ssid" ] && [ "$fg_ssid" = "$a_ssid" ]; then
  fg_ssid=""
fi

# D4: taskid | fg.ssid:<v> | a.ssid:<v>, unresolved segments dropped.
label="$task_id"
[ -n "$fg_ssid" ] && label="$label | fg.ssid:$fg_ssid"
[ -n "$a_ssid" ] && label="$label | a.ssid:$a_ssid"

# The terminal-control port takes the pane (attach, keyed by this session's
# writer id; idempotent) and then writes the label. Either step failing is
# the same silent no-op as every guard above.
key=$(fgos_terminal_key "$project_root")
fgos_terminal_attach "$key" "$HERDR_PANE_ID" || exit 0
fgos_terminal_call label "{\"key\":$(fgos_json_str "$key"),\"display\":{\"label\":$(fgos_json_str "$label")}}" >/dev/null || true
exit 0

name = "fgos-gateway"
version = "0.2.0"
edition = "2021"

[lib]
name = "fgos_gateway"
path = "src/lib.rs"

[[bin]]
name = "fgos-gateway"
path = "src/main.rs"

[dependencies]
serde = { version = "1.0", features = ["derive"] }
serde_json = "1.0"
# tsk-7l9-2 D8: fgos-gateway's first async dependency -- the gateway's REST
# surface (D1/D7) is what needs one; the TUI/orchestrator code stays fully
# synchronous and untouched.
tokio = { version = "1", features = ["rt-multi-thread", "macros", "process", "net", "time", "fs"] }
# tsk-7l9-3: bumped 0.7 -> 0.8 -- required by `rmcp`'s streamable-http-server
# transport (mcp.rs), which only supports axum ^0.8. Breaking route-syntax
# change (`:id` -> `{id}`) rewritten across every existing route in
# gateway.rs's `build_router`; no other breaking change touches this crate
# (State/middleware::from_fn_with_state/Json extraction are unaffected).
axum = "0.8"
# tsk-7l9-3 D1: MCP surface's server SDK -- the official
# modelcontextprotocol/rust-sdk, tokio-async, mounts its
# `transport::streamable_http_server::StreamableHttpService` directly onto an
# existing `axum::Router` via `.nest_service()` (confirmed against the SDK's
# own `examples/servers/src/counter_streamhttp.rs`), so `search`/`execute`
# ride the SAME router/port `tsk-7l9-2`'s REST surface already serves -- no
# second process, no second listener. `mcpkit-axum` (this plan's original
# pick alongside rmcp) turned out to be a wholly separate, non-composable MCP
# SDK (`mcpkit-core`/`mcpkit-server`/`mcpkit-transport`, unrelated to rmcp) --
# dropped, rmcp alone covers the whole surface.
rmcp = { version = "3", features = ["server", "macros", "transport-streamable-http-server", "schemars"] }
# tsk-7l9-3 D1: `execute`'s bound-function scripting language (Approach's own
# rhai-over-mlua pick: pure Rust, no vendored-C/system-Lua dependency, matches
# D1's "no extra runtime layer" rationale). `serde` feature turns bound
# function results (serde_json::Value) into Rhai `Dynamic` values and back.
rhai = { version = "1", features = ["serde"] }
# tsk-7l9-3: `search`'s only new data need -- parses the OpenAPI contract
# (`docs/contracts/fgos-gateway-api-v1.yaml`) into a queryable operation list
# instead of serving it as an opaque string the way `/contract` already does.
serde_yaml = "0.9"
# tsk-54y: CORS layer for `build_router` -- the web client (a separate
# static bundle, D2 of docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard-plan-realignment/
# CONTEXT.md) is not guaranteed to share origin with the gateway. Version
# resolved by `cargo add --dry-run` against this crate's existing axum 0.8
# dependency graph (docs/history/tsk-54y-gateway-cors-bind/plan.md).
tower-http = { version = "0.7", features = ["cors", "fs"] }
# tsk-48w (D14 of docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard-plan-realignment/
# CONTEXT.md): embeds apps/fgos-gateway/web's built bundle into the binary so
# the "máy được chọn" can serve it with no separate deploy step.
# Versions resolved by real `cargo add --dry-run` against this crate's
# existing dependency graph (docs/history/herdr-web-dashboard/plan.md,
# "NẮN LẠI P1 tsk-48w"): rust-embed 8.12.0, axum-embed 0.1.0, same
# rust-embed major line the reference implementation herdr-gateway pins.
rust-embed = { version = "8", features = ["debug-embed"] }
axum-embed = "0.1"
# tsk-6arn (D8): Cloudflare Access as auth layer 2, additive to the
# Bearer token layer already shipped (tsk-7l9). Ported from the reference
# implementation herdr-gateway (crate herdr-go, src/web/cf_access.rs).
# Versions resolved by real `cargo add --dry-run` against this crate's
# existing dependency graph -- differ from the reference's own pins
# (jsonwebtoken 9->11, reqwest 0.12->0.13; reqwest's TLS feature was
# renamed `rustls-tls`->`rustls` between those versions, confirmed by a
# real dry-run failure before the correction). `jsonwebtoken`'s
# `aws_lc_rs` feature is required explicitly -- v11 ships neither crypto
# backend by default (real runtime panic caught at Execute: "Could not
# automatically determine the process-level CryptoProvider... make sure
# exactly one of the 'rust_crypto' and 'aws_lc_rs' features is enabled"),
# and `aws_lc_rs` matches the backend `reqwest`'s own `rustls` feature
# already pulls in, avoiding a second, competing provider in the same
# binary.
jsonwebtoken = { version = "11", default-features = false, features = ["use_pem", "aws_lc_rs"] }
reqwest = { version = "0.13", default-features = false, features = ["json", "rustls"] }
base64 = "0.23"
herdr-fgos-common = { path = "../../packages/herdr-fgos-common/rust" }
fgos-host-runtime = { path = "../../packages/host-runtime/rust" }
fgos-distribution = { path = "../../packages/distribution/rust" }
fgos-git = { path = "../../packages/git/rust" }

[dev-dependencies]
tower = { version = "0.4", features = ["util"] }

- After install, `fgos init` (run inside the target project) → on the npm
  channel it refuses (`git-addon-unavailable: addon not shipped on this
  channel: onboard this project with fgctl init`) and changes nothing: this
  channel ships no native Git addon and Git has one door, so a project is
  onboarded with `fgctl init`, whose activated release carries the addon. The
  init/doctrine/marker-detection behavior itself (owned by the coexistence
  area, see `docs/coexistence.md`) runs from that activated release.

7f9cd7aaaacfccb03bd48531fbb5c81f94704f62.boundText: | 5d | Provider-capacity runtime state | `~/.fgos/runtime/provider-capacity/state.json` — machine-local selected-account lease/quarantine state for provider-capacity rotation. Intentionally host-global only (never project-overridden) so multiple projects sharing provider accounts coordinate concurrency and rate limits safely without starvation. It is never packaged, never committed, and never repaired by `doctor`; `fgos dispatch inspect --provider-capacity` and the `provider-capacity-state` doctor check report it, while manual clear goes through `fgos dispatch reconcile provider-capacity clear-quarantine ...`. An account locked for a dead login is also unlocked by one real call when a dispatch would otherwise find no usable account (the lazy-probe unlock rule, now in `docs/specs/runner.md`). Its locks are holder-lock kernel locks under the machine lock root (row 5g): `provider-state` guards this file, and `provider-account/<provider>/<account>` guards one account while a renewal or unlock probe runs through it, held until that call and every process it started have exited. The same directory holds `account-locks/<provider>/<account>/`: copies of a login renewed elsewhere and waiting to be applied, a scratch home while a renewal runs, and the renewal failure cooldown; it is created only when a renewal or write-back runs and holds no credential outside those copies. | one runtime directory, home-dir-relative | no (created only when a provider account lease/quarantine/write occurs) | absent/inactive |
